note:
digest.digest.is_subscribed: 117 -> 116, and the whole of the -1 is that one field.

`_compute_is_subscribed` resolves `self.env.user` and declared no
`depends_context`, so its cache holds ONE entry per record for the whole
transaction and the first reader's answer is handed to every reader after it.

WHAT THIS IS NOT: a defect anyone was hitting. An earlier draft of this note
claimed `_action_send` reads the field once per recipient. It does not --
grepped across all four repositories, the only readers are
`digest_views.xml`'s `<field name="is_subscribed" invisible="1"/>` and the
module's own tests, and a web request carries one uid. This is the gate's
own case (a compute that resolves `env.user` with an un-keyed cache) closed
because it is cheap and the gate is right about the hazard, not because
something was misbehaving.

Measured per §9.3 against a `git archive` of HEAD, the shared working tree
being unusable for a count (other sessions are holding `addons/loyalty` and
`enterprise/quality`):

  archive of HEAD                     117
  archive of HEAD + digest changes    116   <- committed

`addons/digest/tests/test_digest.py::TestDigestDefects`
::test_is_subscribed_is_the_reader_s_own reads the field as an unsubscribed
user between two reads by a subscribed one, and was observed to fail with the
decorator removed.
